docs.title: What is Grid Play?
docs.text:
Grid Play is a Streamlit-based application that provides a browser interface for:

  • Playing gridworld games with keyboard or button controls
  • Configuring levels with adjustable parameters
  • Testing AI agents through step-by-step execution
  • Creating custom levels using the built-in level editor

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
Grid Play is organized into three main tabs:

Tab Purpose Game Play the game, control your agent, and view your status Config Configure game level State Inspect the full game state for debugging

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
1. Open the Config tab to select a level source
  2. Adjust parameters as desired and click Save
  3. Switch to the Game tab to start playing
  4. Use keyboard controls or buttons to move and interact

docs.title: Config Tab
docs.text: The Config tab lets you select and configure game levels before playing.

docs.title: Level Sources
docs.text:
Grid Play provides two types of level sources:

  • Intro Level Selector
  • Level Editor

docs.title: Intro Level Selector
docs.text:
Pre-designed levels for learning game mechanics.

Source Description Gameplay Example 14 tutorial levels with progressive difficulty

These levels introduce core concepts step-by-step: movement, items, doors, and hazards. Select a level from the dropdown and click Save to play.

docs.title: Level Editor
docs.text:
Configurable levels for experimentation and testing.

Features Usage Level Config Use Width, Height, Seed, Time Limit, Movement Rule, Objective and Agent Health Selector to choose the configuration of the level Entity Pallette, Grid and Preview Use the Entitity Pallete and grid to design the level

Features Usage Level Exporter The Level exporter generates a function to build the designed level

Once done, just click save to proceed to Game Page to test out level.

docs.title: Game Tab
docs.text: The Game tab is where you play and interact with Grid Universe levels. It provides real-time visual feedback, player status, and multiple control options.

docs.title: Interface Layout
docs.text:
The Game tab provide information on the current representation of an ongoing game in the game.

Components Description Left Column Overall Information of the game Middle Column Game View using Observation Class Right Column Agent Control Panel

docs.title: Left Column - Player Status
docs.text:
Displays your current game status:

Indicator Description Total Reward Your accumulated score/reward points Health Points Current HP with damage notifications PowerUp Status Active temporary effects Inventory Items you've collected PowerUp Active Powerups Inventory Collected Items in Inventory

docs.title: Middle Column - Game View
docs.text:
The central area shows:

  • Game Visualization - Real-time rendering of the grid world
  • Observation Info - JSON display of the current game state data

docs.title: Right Column - Game Info
docs.text:
Provides context about your current level:

Section Description New Level Button to generate a new level variant Level Rules Movement type (e.g., cardinal directions) Objective What you need to do to win Turn Counter Remaining turns (if turn limit exists) Agent Control Switch between Button, Keyboard & Code control

docs.title: AI Agent Mode
docs.text: The AI Agent tab allows you to test automated agents:

docs.title: Loading an Agent
docs.text:
1. Click the Settings button to open the agent dialog
  2. Paste your agent code or use the provided template
  3. Click Load to compile and initialize the agent

docs.title: Running the Agent
docs.text:
• Click Step to execute one action from your AI agent
  • The Vision display shows what the agent "sees" using the parse function
  • The Info display shows debug information from your agent using the info function.

docs.title: State Tab
docs.text:
The State tab provides a complete view of the internal game state, useful for debugging, understanding game mechanics, and developing AI agents.

WARNING ON STATE REPRESENTATION

The state page uses the State representation. The Capstone Project can be solved without using the State Representation, however the State Representation is included for a lower level access to the representation.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The State tab displays the full game state as an expanded JSON structure. This includes all internal data that defines the current game situation.
